title: Handoff Granary — Weekly SRE Synthesis (2027-06-18)
content:
Summary:
This week (Mon 2027-06-14 to Fri 2027-06-18) we saw two customer-impacting events (brief P1 and extended P2), several SLO excursions driven by tail latency, and one autoscale misconfiguration surfaced during a staged traffic spike. On-call handoffs were completed without major gaps; noted friction points in escalation steps and runbook clarity.

Incident highlights (short form):
- 2027-06-15 03:42 UTC — P1: GPU worker node flapping in us-west-2 (approx 18m impact to a subset of Dedicated customers). Symptoms: 5xx rate spiked to 3% and p99 generation latency increased >3x for affected pool. Root cause (initial): failing NVLink health checks after a kernel driver bump rolled out to a small batch of nodes. Mitigation: autoscaler drained and replaced nodes, traffic rebalanced to warm fallback pool. Post-incident: rollback of driver update, investigation ticket JIRA-SRE-4021 opened for long-term remediation + regression test.
- 2027-06-16 11:10 UTC — P2: KV cache staleness for hosted API leading to degraded response quality (approx 1h, partial). Symptoms: user reports of hallucinated completions for prompts with heavy prefix reuse; internal metric: cache hit rate dropped 24% for the embedding-prefix cache. Root cause (probable): cache invalidation race when the cache eviction routine ran concurrently with a new serialization format deployment. Mitigation: disabled new eviction path, increased retention TTL for affected keys; follow-up: PR to add stronger invariant tests and a feature-flagged rollout (JIRA-SRE-4030).
- 2027-06-17 14:00 UTC — Staged traffic spike during load test revealed autoscale config error in Dedicated (policy did not account for fractional-GPU ceil behavior). No customer impact in prod but reproduced higher queuing; clarified scaling rule semantics and added unit test to autoscaler logic.

SLOs and metrics snapshot:
- Availability SLO (global hosted endpoint): target 99.95% monthly; rolling 7-day was 99.90% (below target driven mostly by the 06-15 P1).
- Latency SLOs: p95 target < 220ms, p99 < 900ms. This week p95 remained ~210ms but p99 drifted to ~1.15s during incident windows.
- Error budget: remaining monthly error budget now estimated ~0.28%. Early notification to Product & CS.
- Cost signals: autoscaler cooldowns during 06-15 incident caused a temporary spike in fallback usage (higher-cost instance types) — finance notification queued by Solutions Eng.

On-call handoffs & operational notes:
- Handoff cadence: the nightly-to-day shift (02:00 -> 10:00 PT) needs a clearer top-of-shift checklist. Noted that on Tue (06-15) the primary did not confirm fallback pool health before rebalancing which slowed mitigation by ~6 minutes.
- Escalation friction: the escalation matrix step to contact Infra on-call (pager group infra-platform) was ambiguous for driver-level issues. Action: update runbook contact list (see action items).
- War-room tooling: the incident retrospective collated logs from the wrong time window once — investigate runbook helper script that populates timeframe.

Runbook and playbook changes (proposed / in progress):
- kv-cache-playbook: add a dedicated section on "cache-format migrations" and explicit preflight checks when rolling serialization changes — assigned Maria (PR in draft).
- autoscaler: document "fractional GPU ceil" behavior and add unit + integration tests; Noah to own test additions.
- driver-rollout: add kernel/driver rollout gating step and a smoke test that verifies NVLink health on a staged node pool before general rollout — owner Ethan.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- A1: Complete postmortem draft for 06-15 GPU flapping (include timeline, RCA, and mitigation timeline). Owner: Priya. Due: 2027-06-22.
- A2: Add invariant tests and feature-flagged rollout for KV cache eviction change (prevent staging->prod blast). Owner: Maria. Due: 2027-06-25.
- A3: Update on-call runbook contact matrix and add Infra escalation step explicitly. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2027-06-21.
- A4: Autoscaler unit/integration tests for fractional GPU scaling semantics; update config docs. Owner: Noah. Due: 2027-06-24.
- A5: Improve handoff checklist (add quick health-check commands + required screenshot attachments for next shift). Owner: Priya + SRE rotation leads. Due: 2027-06-23.

Meeting notes (weekly SRE sync 2027-06-18):
- Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Maria, Noah, Kira (product), Sam (support).
- Quick wins: rolled back driver canary -> stable; KV cache emergency TTL increased and quality signal recovered.
- Concerns: recurrent p99 tail correlated with cache invalidation and occasional node requeues. Need more observability on per-request cache miss stack traces.
- Decisions: prioritize cache-format tests (high) and autoscaler semantics (medium). Agreed to restrict driver rollouts to 10% canary with NVLink smoke test for next two weeks.

Retro / notes to self (informal):
- The NVLink driver bump probably shouldn't have been in the same batch as other infra changes — keep infra kernel changes isolated.
- Bridge room communication was good, but Slack thread got noisy; try to move core signals to incident channel and summarize in War Room doc.
- We still lack a clean metric that ties "degraded output quality" to specific cache signals — engineering to brainstorm heuristics next week.

Follow-ups for next week:
- Finish and publish postmortem, include customer-facing blurb for CS.
- Run a dedicated tabletop on cache migrations with DevX and Runtime teams.
- Validate the autoscaler fix in staging with progressive rollout.
- Iterate on handoff checklist and runbook automation (small scripts to collect the top 10 health indicators).

Appendix (quick artifacts / links to check):
- JIRA tickets: JIRA-SRE-4021 (GPU node flapping RCA), JIRA-SRE-4030 (kv cache eviction tests), JIRA-OPS-4112 (autoscaler test additions).
- Confluence: kv-cache-playbook (see linked_artifacts above).
- Slack: incident thread (link in linked_artifacts) — contains timeline snippets and customer escalations.

Notes for the next on-call: please verify:
- that fallback pool is warm and has 0 pending NVLink alerts before rebalancing;
- cache hit-rate alarm thresholds are green for the embedding-prefix cache;
- run the health-collect.sh script and attach output to handoff doc.

End of summary.

Quick TODO list (one-liners):
- Postmortem draft (Priya).
- KV feature-flag rollout and tests (Maria).
- Runbook contact update (Ethan).
- Autoscaler test harness (Noah).
- Handoff checklist automation (Priya + rotation leads).

-- Priya K. (on-call lead, week of 2027-06-14)
